chunks: And by his chain, he said,

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) was asked, 'Can one feed the poor with regards to an expiation, the flesh of the sacrifice?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because it is an offering for Allah.'
ai.seo_question: Can the meat of the sacrificial animal for expiating an oath be given to the poor to eat?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies that the meat of the sacrificial animal (udhiyah) used for expiating an oath cannot be given to the poor as their food, because the sacrifice is primarily an offering dedicated to Allah, not merely a source of meat for charity. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of *udhiyah* as a ritual act of worship (*ibadah*) rather than a general charitable gift (*sadaqah*), a distinction preserved in Shia fiqh to maintain the sanctity of the specific ritual offering. The emphasis on 'for Allah' underscores the intentionality required in fulfilling vows and oaths, ensuring the act remains a direct communion with the Divine rather than a utilitarian distribution of resources.

en.hubeali: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was asked, ‘Can one feed the poor with regards to an expiation, the flesh of the sacrifice?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said ;’No, because it is an offering for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 9. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith, the following is narrated: “

’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked, ‘Can the Kaffarah (expiation) because of an oath be fed to the destitute from the flesh of the offering animals for al-Hajj?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, because it is sacrifice for Allah.’”
